source.title: Course 6 - Short-Range Spin Glasses: Selected Open Problems

accepted.question_text: For finite-dimensional Edwards-Anderson short-range Ising spin glass models, where Ising spins take values +1 or -1 on lattice sites and interact through random nearest-neighbor couplings, does a thermodynamic phase transition to a low-temperature spin glass phase occur? Can the Fortuin-Kasteleyn random cluster representation be used to give a rigorous proof of such a phase transition?

For finite-dimensional short-range spin glass models, especially the zero-field Edwards-Anderson model, how many pure thermodynamic states or infinite-volume ground states can occur? In particular, in dimensions greater than one, is the ground-state structure always a single spin-reversal pair, or can there be multiple ground-state pairs?

For realistic finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses, what is the correct mathematical and physical order parameter for the putative low-temperature spin glass phase, and how should it capture the broken symmetry of that phase?

For finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses, what is the effect of applying an external magnetic field on the low-temperature spin glass phase, including the existence or nature of any phase transition and broken-symmetry behavior?

For laboratory and finite-dimensional short-range spin glasses, how should theory account for aging and other anomalous dynamical behavior, especially given slow relaxation and the difficulty of determining whether a system is in or out of equilibrium?

Do the main features of the mean-field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick solution, including Parisi replica symmetry breaking, correctly describe the low-temperature properties of more realistic finite-dimensional short-range spin glass models, particularly their broken symmetry and order parameter?
